judgments.question: Q12
judgments.reason: The answer supplies placement-time harvesting, all three Maker spaces and their base yields, accumulated bonus collection, and Phase 4 addition of one bank spice to spaces without an Agent. Its moved-away sentence is acceptable shorthand in context: the immediately preceding sentence expressly conditions the Phase 4 addition on having no Agent. Read as a whole, the answer does not establish a competing rule that a subsequently reoccupied space receives spice. An additional explicit reoccupation caveat is unnecessary because current occupancy is already stated.

source_refs.supports: Harvesting occurs when an Agent is sent to a Maker space; the gain includes base and accumulated bonus spice.
During Makers, each of the three named spaces receives one bank spice if it has no Agent; spice accumulates.
A vacated Maker space accumulates bonus spice if it remains empty until Phase 4.

judgments.question: Q19 deployment clause
judgments.reason: The clause correctly includes the Combat-space trigger, the two-troop cap, garrison origin, and deployment even without recruits. However, 'may also deploy' permits a discretionary choice to withhold available garrison troops. The automated Rival procedure directs that it also deploys them, subject to availability. This is a material change to the procedure, not merely an omission of the word 'must'; an affirmative formulation such as 'also deploys up to two available garrison troops' would satisfy the rule without any special required terminology.
judgments.scope: This grade assesses the supplied deployment clause only; no other portion of the Q19 answer was supplied for review.

source_refs.supports: House Hagal controls automated Rivals that recruit and deploy troops.
Any time a Rival sends an Agent to a Combat space, it also deploys up to two garrison troops if available, even if the card recruited no troops.
